slides.title: Breakup questions you'd never say out loud

slides.q: Is it a bad idea to hook up with my ex?
slides.a: Not always, but it often reopens the wound. For a lot of people it brings back hope and resets the healing clock. Ask yourself one thing: will I feel okay tomorrow if they still don't want to get back together? If the honest answer is no, it's probably worth skipping. Protect your peace.

slides.q: Should I tell my ex I still love them?
slides.a: Think about what you're hoping happens next. If you want them back and things ended over something fixable, an honest talk can make sense. If it's mostly to get a reaction or closure, it often leaves you hurting more. Writing it down first, or sleeping on it for a week, helps you know for sure.

slides.q: Why can't I focus at work after a breakup?
slides.a: A breakup is a real stressor, and your brain keeps pulling you back to it, which leaves less room for emails and meetings. Poor sleep makes it worse. Short to-do lists, small breaks and being kind to yourself help. It usually eases within weeks. If it drags on for months, talking to someone can really help.

slides.q: Should I go to a party if my ex will be there?
slides.a: You can, if you feel steady enough. Bring a friend who knows the situation, plan how you'll say a quick hello, and give yourself permission to leave early. If you'd spend the whole night watching them, it's okay to skip this one. There will be other parties when it stings less.

slides.q: Is it normal to want to move away after a breakup?
slides.a: Very normal. Everywhere you look holds a memory, so a fresh start sounds amazing. Big moves can be great, but try not to decide in the first few weeks while emotions are loud. A trip, rearranging your room or trying new spots in town can scratch the itch while you figure it out.
